title: Attomicroscopy Imaging of Electron Motion in Action
content: Ultrafast Electron Diffraction and Microscopy imaging have been demonstrated to be pivot tools for imaging the atomic motion in real-time and space [1-3]. The generation of a few hundred femtoseconds electron pulses enabled recording movies for molecular and atomic motion [4]. However, the technical challenges in electron pulse compression have limited the temporal resolution of electron imaging experiments to a hundred femtoseconds. Here, we demonstrate the attosecond temporal resolution in the transmission electron microscope by optical gating [5] to establish what we so-called “attomicroscope” [6]. Moreover, we utilized the attomicroscope to image the electron motion dynamics in graphene. In a strong field, the electron is moving in the reciprocal space following the waveform of the driver field (Fig. 1 A). We conducted an time-resolved attosecond electron diffraction experiment, and we measured the scattered electron intensity modulation, as a function of the time delay between the attosecond electron pulse and the driver field of the pump pulse, of the first, second and third order diffraction peaks (Fig. 1 B). These results allowed us to study the electron density distribution in the reciprocal space at different time instants and connect it with the electron motion in real space (Fig. 1 A). The demonstrated attomicroscopy imaging tool opens the avenue to study electron motion in neutral matter and promises new electron imaging applications in physics, chemistry, and biochemistry [7-9].
